assertion_analysis: tests/test_index_placement.py:48-51 fails if the fleet-runtime default is absent or routed away from ambix/watch-index.sqlite3.
tests/test_index_placement.py:54 fails if the AMBIX_WATCH_INDEX override loses precedence to the fleet default.

tests/test_index_placement.py:55-58 fails if an explicit path is ignored, but the expectation is the same value the test supplied, so an unvalidated echo also passes; locality is proven only by the injected-network cases at lines 72 and 80-86.
tests/test_index_placement.py:72 fails if the runtime candidate is accepted while injected statfs reports GPFS.
tests/test_index_placement.py:78 fails if enable_wal leaves SQLite outside WAL mode on local storage.
tests/test_index_placement.py:80-81 and 82-86 fail if the resolver or enable_wal stops raising on an injected network filesystem; the source run's mutation produced the line-80 failure.
tests/test_index_placement.py:100 fails if the snapshot loses its zst suffix; it does not by itself prove compression.
tests/test_index_placement.py:101-103 fail if backup, compression or restore changes row counts or the SQLite dump digest between the live index and the restored copy.
tests/test_index_placement.py:118-120 fail if four valid snapshots leave other than the newest three, but pruning by filename rather than by verified copies also passes.
tests/test_index_placement.py:137-140 fail if restore chooses a corrupt newest over its predecessor, if the failure is not printed, if the older snapshot is deleted, or if restored counts diverge.
tests/test_index_placement.py:153-162 fail if a damaged same-day snapshot suppresses replacement; the inverse-commit log shows this test red with replacement None.
tests/test_index_placement.py:175 and 180-183 fail if restored catch-up misses the appended receipt, ingests it twice, or diverges from a continuously-ingested index.
tests/test_index_placement.py:193-197 fail if agent watch with no local index errors or does not echo the published file bytes in either output mode.
tests/test_index_placement.py:210-211 fail if the publisher reports success and rewrites the published file; the inverse-commit log shows this test red with the publisher reporting wrote.

findings.text: follow-on: PUBLISHED_WATCH_PATH repeats the value owned by watch_publish.DEFAULT_OUTPUT at imas_ambix/agent/watch_publish.py:47, so a change to one declaration can silently desynchronise the reader from the producer.
follow-on: the explicit-path assertion compares the resolver's return against the same path the test passed in, so it stays true even if require_local stops validating a supplied path.
follow-on: retention is exercised only with valid snapshots, so pruning by filename rather than by verified copies would keep three files and still pass.
follow-on: baseline_suite and after_suite are empty, so the record carries no structured suite-delta receipt although comparable gate logs exist.
